title: Testing multiple viewport sizes
learningObjectives: Explain testing multiple viewport sizes and apply it in an accessible responsive interface.

understand.concept: Responsive testing checks the interface at a range of viewport widths and heights, zoom levels, and content lengths. Use browser responsive tools and real devices where possible. Inspect overflow, navigation, typography, touch targets, focus visibility, and layout transitions.
understand.whyItMatters: A layout that works at one phone width can fail at another. Test just below and above breakpoints, with longer translated text, and with browser zoom or text enlargement.
understand.analogy: Responsive testing is like trying a product in different spaces before shipping it; one successful fit does not prove every size works.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; transforms and animations follow the CSS rendering and timing model.

explain.narrative: This card uses a fluid width and spacing. Test it at several widths and with a longer heading.

examples.expectedOutput: A rendered example demonstrating the relevant responsive or animation behaviour.

practise.guidedTask: Create a viewport test checklist and record results at 320px, 375px, 768px, and 1280px. Fix horizontal overflow and keyboard issues.
practise.independentTask: Build a small example that demonstrates the concept. Check keyboard access and reduced-motion behaviour where relevant.
hints: Test more than one viewport size.
Keep essential information available without motion.
Use developer tools to inspect computed values.

questions.prompt: Why test just above and below a breakpoint?
options: To catch layout changes that fail near the threshold
questions.answer: To catch layout changes that fail near the threshold
questions.explanation: Breakpoint-adjacent widths reveal abrupt layout problems and overflow.

questions.prompt: What should be done for users who prefer reduced motion?
questions.explanation: Respect the user's preference while preserving content and interaction.
